messages:
Sam: Heads up — ran into mismatched invoices for a Dedicated customer. Looks like model fallback + late billing events are producing duplicate charges for the same logical request. Anyone seen this pattern?
Maria: Yup. We've seen routers emit a fallback event and the original event never gets reconciled to a single canonical record. Billing consumers then count both.
Jordan: Two orthogonal problems: duplicate events per request, and attribution that changes after the fact (router -> fallback -> final model). That makes downstream joins messy.
Sam: Proposal: give every billing event a stable request_fingerprint + attribution_state. Emit a short-lived `finalization` event when reconciliation completes. Consumers prefer the finalization record when present.
Maria: SGTM. Also add `attribution_version` and a lightweight `provenance` tag (router|fallback|finalizer) so we can understand transition history.
Ben: Sounds good, but storage/ingest cost is a concern. Finalization events mean more writes. What's the window? customers dispute invoices within 7 days.
Jordan: We don't need to keep everything forever. Make the finalizer async, TTL the transient history (24h-72h) and emit an audit stream for long-term retention only for changed-attribution cases. Most happy-path events are single-write.
Sam: Ingest flow I'm imagining: raw events -> streaming canonicalizer keyed by `request_fingerprint` (de-dup + merge) -> write canonical billing event -> if attribution differs from prior canonical, emit an audit.delta/finalization event.
Maria: Edge: streaming/early tokens. For streaming responses we must tag prefix_id or prefix_fingerprint so token-attribution for partial streams maps back correctly when the final token count arrives. Otherwise token-count reconciliation will be wrong.
Jordan: Example event for conversation:
```json
{"request_id":"RID-abc123","fingerprint":"sha256:...","model":"gptx-8k","tokens":123,"attribution_version":"v2","provenance":"router","finalized":false}
```
Maria: Also: for batched/multi-tenant requests include `tenant_slice_id` and `slice_token_counts` so we can do partial re-attribution without exploding cardinality.
Ben: How do we handle fallback streams that replay tokens (e.g., model A returns first, fallback returns rest)? We must not double-bill overlapping prefixes.
Sam: For overlapping tokens we should store the highest-resolution `seen_prefix_end` per fingerprint and have the canonicalizer compute non-overlapping incremental tokens. If fallback overlaps, canonicalizer subtracts overlap when building final token counts.
Jordan: Practically: add `is_fallback` boolean + `seen_prefix_end` timestamp/offset. Finalizer merges intervals per request_fingerprint to compute final token delta.
Maria: We should be careful about adding nested JSON in events — keep fields flat for Kafka/ClickHouse ingestion, but the consumer can reconstruct boundaries using dot keys like `slice_id` and `tokens_per_slice`.
ops-bot: deploy/ingest-canary: metering-ingest v2 -> staging finished :white_check_mark:
Sam: Action items: Sam -> draft RFC (due Tue), Maria -> prototype schema + streaming canonicalizer patch, Jordan -> spike finalizer job + TTL design, Ben -> run invoice sample sweep for impacted customers.
Maria: One more: instrument a short metric `metering.finalizer.lag_ms` and `metering.duplicate_rate` so we can set SLOs for reconciliation lag and duplicate avoidance.
Jordan: Also add an alert when duplicate_rate > 0.1% over a rolling hour.
Sam: Thanks team — I'll open the RFC and link to this thread. :eyes:
Maria: I'll put a schema sketch in the RFC and include example queries for auditing in ClickHouse.
Ben: I'll carve out time Fri to pull invoices and sample records.
Sam: great — moving to RFC stage.
